assuranceCeiling.rationale: Core F6 target deletion is critical; capture complete cross-namespace dependency provenance and schema role/ACL authority first. This unit is READ-ONLY, has no database connection string and explicitly preserves F6-U03b execution disabled. Proof must identify unknown dependencies rather than silently ignoring their object types.

Static evidence comparator accepts only known external auth.users trigger and exact canonical existing public/private schema ACL sets, and rejects any drift.
Independent read-only query shows exact target database/role, Auth/Storage zero user data, and preserved four buckets; no invocation mutates data.
Workflow and CLI can only render/check query and fixture results; they have no Supabase secrets, connection execution or schema-reset path.
Full exact-head canonical plan, edit-time guards, quality tests, TypeScript, Completion Truth and Lifecycle are enforced; live reset stays BLOCKED.
invariants: Project identity istjjkdcvsvilrycqecd is literal, not caller-overridable in the approved review.
All dependencies with external owner schemas other than the one known Auth trigger block; '?' owner is not ignored.
ACL role grants for public/private are never silently lost or replaced with only CREATE SCHEMA defaults.
No program in the F6-U03d unit may execute hosted DDL or mutate Supabase Auth/Storage/catalog.
Completion Truth may mark the read-only gate's source code ready while destructive deployment and Alap/Pro behavior remain NOT DONE.
forbiddenStates: A live DROP/CREATE executed after a read-only snapshot but before exact transactional revalidation.
A new Supabase-managed external trigger is omitted due to incorrect pg_depend dependent namespace attribution.
The reset compiler drops public/private and recreates them without restoring precise grants to anon/authenticated/service_role/supabase_admin.
A caller substitutes waterk-platform or waterk-staging as the target project.
A source-only test result is reported as proof of 59 hosted customer migrations, live RLS or provider readiness.

failureModes: A pg_trigger dependency is reported with schema '?' and wrongly ignored as not external.
The public schema is recreated without USAGE to anon/authenticated or CREATE to service_role/supabase_admin.
A hidden Auth trigger or managed-view dependency causes unexpected CASCADE removal.
Permissions or catalog changed between read-only query and reset commit.
An untrusted JSON audit report spoofs expected owner or schema ACL values.
A passing offline catalog query is overclaimed as live deployment proof.
edgeCases: Exactly one known Auth.users trigger dependent on private.handle_new_user.
Empty pg_depend relation but missing expected Auth trigger must still BLOCK.
Unresolved dependent class pg_cast or unknown schema owner must BLOCK.
ACL order is normalized, duplicate or extra role grants are rejected.
Public grants: postgres UC, anon U, authenticated U, service_role UC, supabase_admin UC; private grants postgres UC, authenticated U, service_role U.
Unexpected six event-trigger definitions or unknown enabled flags require additional provider-bound safety proof.
Zero Auth users/sessions/storage objects but nonzero business or Office rows must BLOCK.

specialistReviews.finding: App ACL checks are insufficient if six managed event triggers or hidden external dependencies can change schema deletion behavior.
specialistReviews.resolution: Block live reset, enumerate event triggers as unknown until separately verified, require exact in-transaction dependency repeat plus restoration.

specialistReviews.finding: Static empty-row counts and broad pg_depend summaries do not guarantee the actual transaction target.
specialistReviews.resolution: Emit read-only snapshot with scoped identity and normalized dependencies but do not reuse as destructive authorization.

specialistReviews.finding: Dropping public would erase schema ACLs and may disrupt PostgREST Data API even after tables are recreated.
specialistReviews.resolution: Require exact ACL restoration and exposure regression in a subsequent code-gated hosted proof plan; no mutation now.

specialistReviews.finding: A new quality inspector cannot become a parallel fresh-install completion authority.
specialistReviews.resolution: Preserve existing customer-baseline workflow and Completion Truth; source-review verdict is READ_ONLY only.

challenge.scenario: pg_depend output contains thousands of app-owned triggers with schema '?' due to naïve dependent schema classification.
challenge.finding: Misclassifies local dependencies, concealing actual external trigger ownership.
challenge.resolution: Resolve namespace through parent relation for pg_trigger, pg_rewrite, pg_constraint, pg_attrdef and pg_policy; unresolved owner BLOCK.

challenge.scenario: Schema is dropped and recreated with only postgres owner, silently revoking anon/authenticated access.
challenge.finding: CREATE SCHEMA defaults do not restore Supabase's existing schema-level grants.
challenge.resolution: Require exact public/private role-action ACL inventory and a later explicit in-transaction restoration/verification plan before reset can be authorized.

challenge.scenario: auth.users registration trigger gets CASCADE-dropped and never reinstalled.
challenge.finding: One known external Auth trigger references app-private trigger function.
challenge.resolution: Capture exact known external dependency and require later bootstrap restore plus postflight external verification.

challenge.scenario: A managed schema publishes an external view or new FK depending on public, not accounted for in existing F6-U03b guards.
challenge.finding: Checking only foreign keys/triggers is incomplete.
challenge.resolution: Enumerate pg_depend across app namespace/classes and fail closed for unknown externally owned dependent objects.

challenge.scenario: A PG snapshot is passed as valid after Auth user or Storage object appears.
challenge.finding: Historical empty data state cannot authorize future deletion.
challenge.resolution: Read-only report includes current zero-data sentinels and later any destructive implementation must recheck inside the same locked transaction.

challenge.scenario: A fabricated report claims no dependencies and hides the auth.users trigger.
challenge.finding: A count of zero may appear safe but is inconsistent with known target.
challenge.resolution: Require exactly one accepted external dependency with full source and target identity.

challenge.scenario: Unexpected default privileges or event triggers alter behavior during schema reset.
challenge.finding: The previously observed six event triggers and namespace ACLs require distinct inspection.
challenge.resolution: Record event-trigger names/definitions and force future review of their effects; never infer readiness from ACL check alone.

challenge.scenario: GitHub workflow accidentally receives Supabase secrets and uses psql despite offline intent.
challenge.finding: Quality authority must be separated from hosted target execution.
challenge.resolution: Compile/test static query contract without secrets or psql invocation; live snapshot reads happen only via approved Supabase read-only connector.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: Current occupied disposable Supabase target has 175 public + two private tables, with one known external auth.users trigger depending on private.handle_new_user and schema-level ACLs not restored by the historical F6-U03b proposed DROP/CREATE. Destructive replay must remain prohibited until the full live target dependency, ACL, role, user-data and managed-schema boundary is demonstrably checked.
observableOutcomes: A read-only PostgreSQL catalog SQL report enumerates every cross-schema application-owned dependency with correctly resolved owner namespaces for pg_trigger, pg_rewrite, pg_constraint, pg_attrdef, pg_policy, pg_proc, pg_class, pg_type and pg_namespace.
The only accepted external dependency is the exact auth.users/on_auth_user_created -> private.handle_new_user trigger. Unknown, unresolved, extension-owned or system-dependent edges block.

The exact schema ACL sets for public and private, owners and service-role/anon/authenticated grants are captured, checked and required for any future reconstructed public/private schema. Existing destructive compiler still has hard fail-before-DROP.
Evidence reports only READ_ONLY_BLOCKED_RESET and limited catalog/readiness scope, never full hosted Fresh Install, COMMIT, 59 migrations or Alap/Pro RLS PASS.
Existing project states remain two ACTIVE (platform and Fresh Install) and staging INACTIVE; no Supabase SQL writes or credential access.
unresolvedRisks: Snapshot SQL runs read-only, so it cannot guarantee no data or dependency drift between observation and any future destructive transaction; in-transaction locks and identical guards are still required.
The six observed Supabase PostgreSQL event triggers may fire on schema creation/deletion; their safety remains unproved until separate explicit inspection and fault testing.
Schema ACLs alone do not establish all table/view/function grants, default privileges, PostgREST exposure or Auth worker behavior after recreation.
An application's later live 59-file migration run and genuine signed-in role RLS proof remain separately blocking.
